text:
🪿 u are not ur own audience.

most people don't think like u. be careful building for urself.

🪿 nobody buys "the art of filmmaking."
everybody buys "making $5K with it."

🪿 put ur freebies straight into the free community.

it almost replaces a funnel.

🪿 answer every member question and they stop trying to figure it out themselves.

u also burn urself out.
🪿 ur paid offer is always a more refined version of ur free offer.

🪿 sell the one-on-one.
deliver the group call.

less pressure on u, less pressure on them, and everyone learns from the same feedback.

🪿 leave room for haters.

if nobody's outside of ur community, it's not a community.

🪿 prices drop at an extra digit.

$9 works. $10 doesn't.
$99 works. $100 doesn't.
$999 works. $1,000 doesn't.

🪿 one-on-ones are what people think they want.

they're also the lowest-ROI way to share information.

🪿 ur Gucci tracksuit has buy buttons and logos everywhere.
don't let ur community look like that.

🪿 if u're doing high ticket, do high high ticket.

$5K for one visit. don't go lower.

🪿 don't build the whole thing first and then go find people.

find people. ask what their problem is. fix it with them. keep going.

🪿 "i'll visit u twice a year for $10,000."

can't afford it? "i'll visit u once for $5,000."

🪿 the best anchor offers are so good they're cringy. "abs in 30 days." "meet ur soulmate in 30 days."

they sound terrible, and nothing sells better.

🪿 the app isn't the goal.
the money is.

if u can get there with an app, great. if not, find another way.

🪿 people found the community and cared less about the app.

lean into where they actually hang out.

🪿 the most engaged anyone will ever be is the moment they join.

that's ur activation point. use it.

🪿 new member onboarding:

answer 3 people's problems today.

that's it. that's all u gotta do.

🪿 teach them to comment first.
then teach them to post.
then give them a treat.

that works wonders.

🪿 launching a third space means hiring more people or splitting ur time.

that eats the margin u just made.

🪿 before u launch a third community,
double the clients in the one that already works.

🪿 give value away for free first.
earn the trust and respect.

then ask for money.

🪿 the free phase is data.

ask the market what they actually need before u sell it.

🪿 people pay when there's a clear point of action.

show them the next step.

🪿 a $1,000 offer. a $200 offer. a $9 offer.

u just gave urself a way out of the result u wanted.

🪿 free community first.
give insane value.
then put the high ticket on the back end.

🪿 want to monetize faster?

give people fewer ctas.

🪿 free, premium, vip, one offer?

do not overcomplicate this.
one offer.

🪿 plant ur flag on a time that works for u.

if people want to come, they can come.

🪿 ur audience is defined by who u are.

who u consistently want to be is who finds u.
🪿 there's a difference between service and sacrifice.

🪿 chasing an audience is exhausting.

attract them instead.

🪿 u'll never hit every hour ur members are online.

"when can i best be available?" is a losing question.

🪿 make ur life easy first.

when ur life is easy, u can make theirs easier too.

🪿 if u struggle with a thing,
u might be really good at teaching it.

u'll be banging ur head against it longer than anyone.

🪿 tidying ur pillows for the image of who u think ur supposed to be?

that's digging ur own grave.
🪿 people sign up for things because they're easier, faster, or lower risk.

🪿 hit them with too many angles
and all u create is overwhelm.

🪿 a beginner course.
a game every month.
a call once a week.

that's it. leave them wanting more.

🪿 what's a free community for?

to turn people into ur ICP.
🪿 over-deliver in a way people can digest easily.

🪿 make ur members feel something.

put a little of ur heart and time into it.
🪿 there are few things as powerful as something physical that u can give a member of ur community.

🪿 can't keep a tracker?

connect a google sheet to ChatGPT or Claude.

then just say "hey i just did this."

even a voice memo works.

🪿 most people can't keep a tracker for months.

probably 95% of them.

u either grow insane discipline or u remove the friction.

🪿 i'm not a fan of throwing extra discipline at it.

making it easier or making it fun is usually my strategy.

🪿 low ticket is easier.

it usually doesn't take care of u quite as well.

🪿 most people jump on the next offer the second it looks like money.

the smart ones pause.

🪿 know ur financial goal.

then work it backwards.

otherwise u're signing up for golden handcuffs.

🪿 3 questions before u build a high ticket:

what do u enjoy doing?
who do u enjoy doing it with?
what are the variations of it?

🪿 the biggest earners i know still plan.

they sit down and map out what they might launch and in what order.

🪿 u don't get freedom by purely making the money.

money from work u hate is just a hamster wheel.

🪿 the day u truly believe u deserve the price,
u'll probably start to see results.

🪿 u probably do a really good job with what u do.

maybe better than u know.

🪿 the hard part usually isn't delivering.

it's saying the number out loud.

🪿 don't give the welcome gift away on join.

make members earn it.

they'll post pics with it.

🪿 include something funny that has nothing to do with what u do.

that's what makes it charming.

🪿 start with a paid community?

not unless u have 100k+ followers.

if they're not primed, start free.

🪿 when ur living it out loud, people feel it.

they're learning from exactly what u're going through.

🪿 busy people join, get their results, and leave.

u need a reason for them to come back to the community.

🪿 u don't have to write a three-page letter.

but a little handwritten note goes a long way.

🪿 focus on one community.
managing two doubles your labor and your offers.
keep the juice in one place.

🪿 a $21 or $27 price tag means u need a massive crowd.
one higher-priced offer is far less work.

🪿 over-delivering on cheap offers will run u ragged.
keep the price in line with the work.

🪿 give free value, then present a single clear offer.
upsells become way easier.
🪿 find the signal, double down on it, then slap a clear call-to-action.
🪿 they think they want the supplier, but they really need a healthy protocol - sell the protocol, not the source.
🪿 anyone can google a peptide supplier; your edge is what to do with that information.
🪿 give real value first, earn goodwill, and watch free members upgrade to paid.
🪿 lock the good stuff right after a trial and u lose them; keep the door open, charge for premium tools.

🪿 be opinionated, keep it brief
that's the sweet spot for comments.

🪿 if u promise easier, faster, lower risk
they'll pick u over the competition.

🪿 poke fun at the misery we all share
the insiders will hit that like button.

🪿 they say they want a custom url
what they actually need is a self filtering community.

🪿 a free community is a bootcamp for your ICP
once they're trained, they upgrade like clockwork.
🪿 activation point: give a new member a win in the first 20-60 minutes and they'll stick around.
🪿 u can keep free marketing forever, but without a clear upgrade deadline the urgency disappears.

🪿 narrow your offer to one thing.
voice ai, video ai, or prompt generators.
people choose a specialist over a jack-of-all.

🪿 when members skip the action, it's on u.
encourage the right behavior, don't blame them.

🪿 live demos grab attention, but don't give the whole recipe away.
show a scribble turn into magic, then sell the process.

🪿 sell the result, not the steps.
"build a digital business fast" beats "learn ai tool basics".

🪿 if ur content takes more than 45 minutes to make, it's not simple enough.
trim it down.

🪿 throw out 3-5 versions.
one or two will hit the signal, then crank out more.
🪿 a thousand views feels tiny to some, but for u it's proof u've got an audience.

🪿 start with "what's ur main goal?" and "what's ur biggest pain?"
if it's not a fit, u'll know fast.

🪿 people buy "more done in less time."
price your program as a time-saver, not a course.

🪿 before u tweak anything, lock in a baseline.
collect a week or a month of cold, hard numbers.
use that as your anchor.

🪿 nurture free members then ascend them.
drop a paid call into the free group once or twice a month.
they get a taste without extra work.

🪿 weekly calls work best.
overdelivering can make members think they're missing weeks.
keep the rhythm steady.

🪿 test one variation at a time.
give each change a month to prove itself.
clean data beats chaos.
🪿 what makes u weird is what makes u stand out.
🪿 u can't sell authenticity, u can only model it.
🪿 authenticity shows up when u let others see u being weird.

🪿 inside jokes are the secret sauce
that turns a group into a real community.

🪿 shared purpose + frequent interaction = any coach;
only inside jokes make it a community.

🪿 inside jokes add love, not labor,
and that love fuels recurring revenue.

🪿 inside jokes keep members sticking around longer
and boost their lifetime value.
🪿 retention = tool + inside jokes.

🪿 want to monetize?
pair the fun community with a usable tool.

🪿 tool doesn't have to be a full app.
a spreadsheet or a GHL snapshot works.
🪿 lazy 80-20 rule: grab the quickest, easiest ROI tool and roll it out.

🪿 complicated software? nope.
keep the tool simple and digestible.

🪿 hit both marks - inside joke + cta -
and u score bonus points
every single time.

🪿 if your name isn't a cta,
people will ask,
"what does this community do?"

🪿 having a plan b?
that means u ain't committed.
burn the ships.

🪿 perfect momentum is a myth.
either full send it now or stay stuck.

🪿 two options only:
 u're making excuses or u don't actually want it.
🪿 the best teachers are the ones who struggle with the same problem the most.

🪿 pain's inevitable.
either let it happen to u or choose ur own pain.

🪿 cultivate inside jokes by taking urself less seriously
stupid, silly, weird wins

🪿 a stilted community feels sustainable but dies fast
keep it alive with realness

🪿 mess up on camera? keep it
those moments are authenticity gold
🪿 authenticity isn't a buzzword; it's the habit of never deleting the ugly bits

🪿 focus on your own stuff.
copycats drain your energy.

🪿 best revenge is success.
let them watch u win.

🪿 people will always copy your product.
that's just reality.

🪿 the only thing they can't steal is u.
your personality, your style.

🪿 the more successful u get, the more copycats show up.
expect it.

🪿 they can mimic the roadmap, not the creator.
u stay unique.

🪿 three years from now u'll forget the copycat.
u're too busy winning.

🪿 the trial only needs one thing: keep them comfortable enough to stay.
no extra tasks required.

🪿 picture yourself a year out as a community leader.
that future u will sell with confidence, not panic.

🪿 bundle the random tools u already give them into "the thing".
even a rough package gives them something to hold.
🪿 shift your mindset: u're not just a free host, u're the person they need to make life easier - sell that.

🪿 paid members are paying for direct access to u.
that's the only thing that matters long term.

🪿 let a team member run the challenge.
u just pop in for the celebrity intro.

🪿 expect your high-ticket group to dip while the free one climbs.
let the free crowd carry the star.

🪿 lower barrier = higher conversion.
free leaderboard beats paid low-traffic board.
🪿 ditch the fancy curriculum. all u need is an activation point and daily accountability

🪿 keep it free until it's painful.
that way u don't choke growth early.

🪿 jump to paid too fast and u'll strangle your own funnel.
slow burn wins.

🪿 u can't teach a service u haven't done.
experience first, education later.

🪿 give massive free value.
collect case studies.
watch paid offers appear.

🪿 deliver results consistently.
people will ask, "can i pay u for this?"
🪿 u'll need to monetize eventually, but only after u've proven it works.

🪿 think of the free group as a funnel.
feed it, then sell the service when the demand's real.
🪿 to optimize for community u gotta be unprofessional. drop the corporate mask.
🪿 inside jokes = the single biggest community driver. if u don't have them, u've missed the point.
🪿 being overly professional scares people off. let your weird side shine.
🪿 your only unique selling point is u. live it in every interaction.

🪿 turn off membership questions.
auto-approve everyone.
conversion jumps.

🪿 level two onboarding lets new members feel the vibe first.
no spam, just culture.

🪿 high-ticket clients crave accountability.
 give them small goals and regular check-ins and watch them bite.

🪿 don't ask them to join the community.
 show the value first, they'll hop on when they see it.

🪿 start with weekly challenges and feedback loops.
 constant hype kills engagement.

🪿 most high-ticket buyers hand over cash, not time.
 keep it simple: accountability, no fluff.

🪿 think of tiers like basketball seats.
cheap seats see the game, courtside is extra.
u can enjoy the game without the box.

🪿 if u keep premium talks visible, it creates natural FOMO.
people see snippets and want more.

🪿 separating free and paid into different groups doubles your workload.
 u're pushing a bigger boulder up the mountain.
🪿 paid members aren't buying a whole new experience, just a little extra and gratitude included.

🪿 u don't need to make the paid tier "so much more valuable."
they already get what they pay for plus the free value.

🪿 the single vertical model: same audience, different level of service.
no need for separate communities.

🪿 give everything away for free.
people will send u cash later.

🪿 your high-ticket offer can be just your phone number.
accountability sells better than info.

🪿 money-rich folks lack time.
they pay for your hand-holding.

🪿 stop splitting free vs paid.
just share it all and watch stickiness grow.

🪿 action beats perfection.
the ones who try are the winners.

🪿 generosity builds community stickiness.
people stay when u give them everything.

🪿 the best offers aren't info, they're accountability.
people pay for your time, not your knowledge.

🪿 give ur community a 30-day challenge.
one tiny task each day.
they check in, they get hooked.

🪿 when the whole group finishes the daily tasks,
they unlock a course together.
collaboration becomes the reward.

🪿 keep the daily action under five minutes.
hold them accountable, give a nudge,
they'll actually do it.

🪿 there's no magic formula.
just a loose script
and a lot of riffing.

🪿 don't try to be everyone.
let introverts do introvert ads,
moms do mom ads,
niche wins.

🪿 chaos = gold.
shoot where u can't control the scene
and watch it become the most interesting ad.

🪿 give yourself constraints.
they force fun ideas
and there's no wrong answer.

🪿 the stupid, messed-up ads
often become the top performers.
have fun, it works.

🪿 play > polish.
if u're having fun, the ad will land.

🪿 vulnerability opens the door.
when u show up raw,
the whole group mirrors it.

🪿 be anti-professional.
the moment u drop the act,
results actually rise.

🪿 repeat until it sticks.
u say it once,
u say it twice,
u say it till they get it.

🪿 courses are perfect bait.
people will buy them,
then they forget they exist.

🪿 sell them what they want,
then give them what they need.

🪿 broccoli wrapped in bacon.
wrap the medicine in something tasty,
they swallow both.

🪿 run a pointless competition.
it looks silly,
but while they play,
they're actually moving forward.

🪿 use your real face.
no secondary mask,
the community feels professional.

🪿 front-door friction kills growth.
 drop the questions, let them in instantly.

🪿 bots are a pain, not a death sentence.
 let them flood in, then hunt them down for fun.

🪿 let anyone in, qualify later.
 free entry fuels a bigger pool of qualified leads.

🪿 granular onboarding works:
 post a comment, earn five likes, unlock the next module.

🪿 level three is the sweet spot.
 once members hit it, engagement spikes.
🪿 they think money, sex, abs = happiness. they don't. they need a system for real joy.
🪿 speak their language: health, wealth, relationships. promise more cash or six-pack, deliver happiness.
🪿 your offer is a mask. say "more money", secretly teach "how to be happy". they buy the mask.
🪿 your about page sells the results they think they want, not your story. keep the focus on them.
🪿 the biggest hang-up: getting stuck on the offer because it feels not like u. ignore the feeling, launch anyway.

🪿 money-making niche = fraction of the right people.
relationship niche = almost all the right people.

🪿 before anything, nail the vibe of your ICP.
business details come later.

🪿 pick a theme.
it sparks a feeling.
inside jokes grow.

🪿 why settle for a boring business community?
make it feel like a riot.

🪿 theme is one of Skool's top three underused tools.
use it.

🪿 what vibe do u want people to walk into?
pick a movie, cartoon, or mystery novel that gives it.

🪿 people don't know what they want.
stop asking them.

🪿 level 1 chase money, sex, abs.
what they really need? a community that reflects them.
🪿 confidence that u can deliver = no need to ask for consent.

🪿 stop framing it as a question.
say "we're adding this" and watch them nod.
🪿 remove friction, give the benefit, and they'll say yes without thinking.
🪿 community is the mirror that shows u what u actually need.

🪿 when your fix pays for itself in weeks, charge high-ticket.
value outpaces cost, period.

🪿 a moving-target offer gets zero replies.
freeze the promise into a single, bold claim.

🪿 most people say they want info.
what they really want is more access to u.

🪿 they'll buy the course.
they won't use it.
they'll hang out in the community.

🪿 thank the people u learn from publicly.

they'll be happy u're talking about them. then flex the thing u can now do.

🪿 value and practical stuff matter in a community.

but don't forget how practical the other stuff is.

easter eggs. inside jokes. the stupid shit.

🪿 on social media there's a hump.

it feels weird and out there until u find the few weirdos who say "i do this too, i just never recorded it."

🪿 members are forgiving.

they barely remember what u promised at launch, as long as u keep delivering.

🪿 at our IRLs, the people who aren't from Skool are always amped.

they bring a really powerful energy.

🪿 want to share ur coaching calls with a cheaper offer? ask ur high-ticket members for permission.

most say yes. if they don't, u haven't worked on the culture enough yet.

🪿 when a community finds something that works, it gets scared to lose it.

so it stops building and starts holding on.

that's when it falls apart.

🪿 get a few people obsessed with the same thing, each testing a different variation.

only one of u has to test it to teach the rest.

🪿 i tried platform after platform with all the features i thought i wanted.

then i got to Skool and realized i just needed simple.
🪿 a lot of the time u're hired as a coach to trick ur clients into doing the thing they already know they should be doing.

🪿 in a community, the question isn't how much u made this month.

it's churn and LTV. how long are u going to spend ur life with these people?

🪿 waiting for someone to hold the camera?

u're never going to control ur environment. learn to summon it from urself anyway.

🪿 if all u want is short-term money, Skool might not be the play.

community takes time.

🪿 the best part of an IRL isn't meeting people.

it's being in a room where u don't have to explain urself.

🪿 whatever u're saying in a DM, if u can say it in one or two lines, do that.

short and to the point beats cute.

🪿 my first community was all about traffic and conversions.

then everyone liked me more than the brand.

so i made the community an extension of me.

🪿 charging for it makes it less fun.

not charging gets u people who aren't qualified.

best of both worlds: a group where the leaderboard is the metric.

🪿 every ad has three parts. the hook. the body. the CTA.

shoot a bunch of hooks and swap them in.

🪿 starting out, u have no people, no proof, no testimonials.

the fix: 5-10 people, one week, one quick win on day one. then plan nothing and just get them talking.

🪿 u don't need a lot of approval.

some disagreement is helpful. it means what ur doing is changing minds.

do it gently.

🪿 one outsider in the room and the activity picks up.

they ask the boring, "stupid" questions. most people learn the most when they're teaching.

🪿 engagement runs on emotion and enthusiasm.

it can't thrive off the same activity over and over.

🪿 using someone else's platform feels like doing someone else's thing.

that's why i didn't sign up for Skool at first.

then a lot of people get in and find the progress comes just from being present.

🪿 if it's not fun for me, why the hell would i buy it?

gamify what's good for ur client and u've kind of hacked it for them.

🪿 homework: shoot three videos holding the camera urself.

backyard, house, the store. the store scores extra points.

if it's uncomfortable, u're growing.

🪿 sometimes the people u love most are the biggest resistance to the thing u feel u have to build.

find people with the same ailments. it's wind in ur sails.

🪿 one block message is less trustworthy than individual lines.

a block can be perfected. lines with typos feel raw and authentic.

we tested it: 20-30% higher response.

🪿 there's a point where u stop being the manager and become a community leader.

that's when u want to see ur members benefit.

🪿 don't ask for a testimonial in a DM afterwards.

on the last day, ask what their experience was and what helped most. one person at a time while everyone listens.

it's 10x better.

🪿 a testimonial montage is one line to open, a row of wins, and one line to close.

five seconds a person.

🪿 lifetime members go quiet the fastest.

if i've already paid forever, i've got no reason to show up.

🪿 when someone joins ur community, don't dump years of what u've learned on them in the first step.

that overwhelms people. make every step tiny.

🪿 never use oversaturation as the reason not to do a thing.

ask first: do i enjoy this? do i have any leverage in this space yet?

🪿 if ur community name describes the process, it's the wrong name.

people don't want the process. they want the result.

🪿 kicking out inactive members doesn't help ur ranking.

it probably hurts u too. u lose the chance to reactivate them.

🪿 when u price ur community, if u're comfortable with the number, it's probably too low.

a little uncomfortable is good.

🪿 left alone, we'll build the perfect course for months and never finish it.

instead, run it live with a few people for a week and record it.

🪿 give the course away as a lead magnet.

the calls and the community are what keep them. nobody realizes yet that's what they want.

🪿 if nobody's showing up to ur free calls, don't start charging for them.

🪿 name ur community after the place people go when they have the problem.

struggling in ur marriage? the marriage school.

🪿 people only buy health, wealth, or relationships.

and only the dramatic version. they don't buy friends. they buy soulmates.

🪿 keep paid and free members in the same space.

the free ones get FOMO for the paid ones, and more of them upgrade.

🪿 if the only reward in ur community is money, u get lightning engagement.

🪿 u don't know what u need from a community platform until u've actually used one.

the features i was sure i wanted weren't it.

🪿 clients buy the result.

what they actually need is a cool, fun roadmap.

🪿 "i don't have to explain myself." it's the thing people talk about the most after an event.

for most of ur life, u do.

🪿 if i get a DM longer than three lines, i usually ignore it.

it's going to take a while and it's usually a pitch.

🪿 in my community, the stupid jokes and random stuff are why people stay.

the traffic and conversions talk happens on the back end.

🪿 in an ad, some hooks are better. some bodies work better with certain hooks.

so shoot a bunch of each and mix them.

🪿 u can't just decide to be happy.

u do something u enjoy so much that happiness follows. community works the same way.

🪿 if it takes u longer than a week to get ur course out, ur head's up ur ass.

record it live with a few people and ship it.

🪿 growing a mastermind? keep everyone in the free community at first.

the FOMO u can create there takes very little effort.

🪿 search ur niche and see a bunch of tiny communities?

that's data. u're not looking at the wrong platform, u're looking at the wrong niche.

🪿 give free value on a call and u might walk out with a client.

that's how it happens in a Skool community. on calls and in the regular chat.

🪿 the information is free or cheap.

what they're really paying for is access to u and ur leadership.

🪿 as u scale, u're granting more access: easier, faster, lower risk.

that's why people pay u more.

🪿 build momentum in one community first.

get to 500 activities a day there before u start splitting into more.

🪿 give people so much value that when it's time to charge, they're looking forward to it as much as u are.

🪿 ur lead magnet is just the front door.

what's inside can be a bunch of other stuff that has nothing to do with it.

🪿 stop trying to be a particular person or run a particular strategy.

put as much of ur weirdness into the ad as u can and see what lands.

🪿 end the testimonial montage with one line: "we're here to make sure that happens to u too."

nothing's more powerful than a row of wins back to back.

it needs new customers nonstop. community keeps the ones u already have.

🪿 ur community's front page should promise the result they'll get.

the inside should be all the fun. merge those and people don't leave.

that's an opportunity. every new eyeball is a brand new eyeball.

🪿 if ur community name sounds like work, it's the wrong name.

it should feel like the place u go to get the one thing u really want.

🪿 if u're thinking about how to manipulate ur community's engagement, ur energy is in the wrong place.

get more people in and more people taking action.

if u coach dating, u set up their profile on day one.
